blocks.title: FigCraft in the activity panel
blocks.description: Frames, auto layout, components and variables — the upstream FigCraft editor running inside Astravia, on the file you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: Open FigCraft and turn the background of @assets/cover.png into a blue gradient.
showcase.assistant_reply: Cover loaded. Turning the background into a blue gradient now.

items.title: Frames and auto layout
items.description: Layout is a property of the frame, so a list stays a list when its text changes — the same model the file expects, not absolute pixels.

items.title: Components and variables
items.description: Components, variants and variables let one change reach every instance, which is what keeps a design file from drifting into fifteen near-copies.

items.title: Prototypes you can point at
items.description: A capture tool shows what the canvas is displaying and a status tool reports whether the editor finished starting, so a prototype is checked, not described.

items.title: Driven from the conversation
items.description: Ask in chat and the panel carries it out: pointer and keyboard steps run inside the editor one after another, each one named on the canvas while it happens.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 10 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that.

items.title: Open the FigCraft tab
items.description: Opening the tab shows the editor itself — no preparation screen, no package to fetch.

items.title: Select the design file, then open it
items.description: File → Open inside the editor takes the file selected in Astravia.

items.title: Export back through the workspace
items.description: Exports travel the same bridge as saves.

blocks.content: FigCraft is pre-1.0: the file format and some editing behaviour are still moving. The plugin runs the pinned release and adds no design features of its own.

Automation is an ordinary operation, not a macro player: a batch is a list of pointer and key steps the editor receives exactly as if they came from a hand, paced by frames so a press lasts a press. The canvas reports a text map and its average colour back, which is how the agent checks that a change really happened before reporting it.
